title: The button
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: A button gone on the coat. On the desk in the morning: a button that doesn't match, sewn on, the thread a different brown. The mother's hand did it in the night. The strip draws the button and not the hand. The coat has its mismatch now. It keeps it till 2011.

panels.composition: The chore coat on the chair, morning. Where a button was: a button. Wrong. Bigger, darker, sewn tight with a different thread.

image.prompt: close on a canvas chore coat draped over a chair with one button larger and darker than the rest, sewn on with mismatched thread, black and white, no words

panels.composition: WOOD's thumb on the button. Turning it. Tight.

image.prompt: close on a young man's thumb testing a mismatched button on a coat, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood looking at the door. The hall. No one. BARNABY on the bed. The hand isn't in this strip. The strip draws the door.

image.prompt: a young man in a bedroom looking at an empty doorway, a small dog on the bed, a coat over a chair, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood in the coat, the mismatched button done up. Out the door. Fast. The strip drawn faster: sixty strokes. The button is one of them.

image.prompt: a young man in a chore coat with one mismatched button walking out a door, drawn in sixty sparse strokes, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen over rough blue pencil; xerox grain; stark spotting; rain in frantic vertical hatching (Arc 1's aesthetic)

notes: The mismatched button. The hand isn't in the strip; the door is. Kept till 2011.
